key_features.classic_presentation: Mesenteric ischemia presents with sudden-onset severe periumbilical pain out of proportion to physical exam findings. Patient appears very uncomfortable but abdomen may be soft initially. High mortality if delayed diagnosis.
key_features.typical_demographics: Elderly (>60 years), atrial fibrillation, vascular disease, recent MI. Very rare in young patients without risk factors.
key_features.pathophysiology_brief: Arterial embolism, thrombosis, or non-occlusive ischemia causes bowel infarction.

diagnostic_questions.question_focus: pain out of proportion to exam
diagnostic_questions.context: Classic finding: severe pain but benign abdominal exam initially.
Very rare without vascular risk factors. Age >60 + AF = high risk.
Sudden onset if embolic, more gradual if thrombotic.
Late finding (indicates bowel infarction already occurred).

red_flags.action: Mortality 60-80% if delayed. Immediate surgical consultation required.

typical_management: Emergency surgery, vascular intervention, anticoagulation. Early diagnosis critical for survival.
disposition: Emergency department, immediate surgical consultation, likely ICU.
patient_education: This is a life-threatening emergency requiring immediate surgery.
